definition: Shape coding is a visual processing mechanism that represents the overall form or pattern of items, helping people quickly estimate small numbers by matching what they see to familiar shape-like arrangements. In this context, it refers to how the organization of elements into simple shapes can support numerosity judgments.

reasons: The definition claims shape coding “represents the overall form or pattern of items.” The packet only mentions “shape-template matching” and selectivity to visual features; it does not explicitly describe shape coding as representing overall form/pattern.

The definition states it “help[s] people quickly estimate small numbers by matching what they see to familiar shape-like arrangements.” The packet supports facilitation of numerosity estimation around the subitizing range via shape-template matching, but does not support “matching to familiar shape-like arrangements.”

The definition ties shape coding to “how the organization of elements into simple shapes can support numerosity judgments.” The packet does show target arrangements on “vertices of simple shapes” and improved performance in some conditions, but the specific general phrasing about “organization … into simple shapes” is not fully grounded as a defining mechanism of shape coding in the packet.
Because the definition includes substantive claims that are not directly supported by the supplied packet, it should be rejected.
